clue.text: Very keen on alcoholic drink that's passed round at feast

definitions.text: drink that's passed round at feast

parts.note: loving something means being very keen on it
a cup is a mixed alcoholic drink, such as claret cup or fruit cup

explanation.surface: Someone fond of drink eyes the bowl being handed about at a banquet.
explanation.walkthrough: A CUP is a punch-like mixed drink, so 'alcoholic' stands for it here; the LOVING CUP is a large shared vessel passed between guests at a formal dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-handled communal goblet circulated among diners at ceremonial banquets for each to sip in turn.

clue.text: Bound to get a lot of scurvy treatment with it

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most of it, so its final letter is dropped here

parts.note: limes were issued to sailors to prevent scurvy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor's cure for scurvy is taken along with something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims LIME to LIM. British sailors were given lime juice against scurvy, hence 'limeys'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound is a boundary or furthest extent, a synonym for the noun meaning the point beyond which one cannot go.

clue.text: Avant-garde surrealist's mark seen in deliberate damage

parts.note: the van, short for vanguard, is the front line, as avant-garde means
Salvador Dali was the famous Spanish surrealist painter, and the 's gives its S
M is the abbreviation for the German mark currency

explanation.surface: A modern painter's signature is spotted on a wilfully defaced wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilful destruction of property, the crime of smashing or defacing things on purpose.

clue.text: Honour civic head, we hear, in appalling situation

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the words are said aloud and spelt as they sound

parts.note: a knighthood is an honour, and a mayor is the head of a town council

explanation.surface: Knighting the town's leader turns out to be a disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: KNIGHT (an honour) and MAYOR (civic head) said aloud give the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrifying or awful experience, figuratively a bad dream come true.

clue.text: Blow up elite — anarchist's dreams

indicators.note: blowing something up shatters it, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

parts.note: here the possessive's S is used as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A bomber plans to explode the ruling class, dreaming of revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow up' shuffles ELITE and ANARCHISTS (fifteen letters, the S included).
explanation.definitionFit: Idle fantasies or daydreams that have no foundation in reality.

clue.text: There's no stopping what cranky inventors come up with

definitions.text: There's no stopping what cranky inventors come up with

parts.words: There's no stopping what cranky inventors come up with
parts.note: reads as exasperation at endless crackpot ideas, but describes a machine that, as claimed by eccentric inventors, runs forever without stopping

explanation.surface: Eccentric inventors keep producing ideas without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A supposed machine that keeps running indefinitely without any energy input, a classic dream of crank inventors.

clue.text: Good in bed, but get into trouble

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as the clue's 'in' tells us

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
PI, short for pious, is the crossword abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A lover is excellent between the sheets, yet lands in hot water.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for being punished or getting into serious trouble.

clue.text: Ready to say where valuables are hidden

indicators.note: to say something is to speak it, so the word is spelt as it is heard

parts.note: ready money, or 'the readies', is cash

explanation.surface: Someone is prepared to reveal where the treasure is stashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like an adjective, but 'the ready' is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden store or stash of treasure or supplies.

clue.text: Artist's little boy has to pose for a start

indicators.note: puts the word for pose at the beginning, ahead of the word before it

parts.note: to put a question is to pose it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter's young son must model first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a start' moves PUT (pose, as in putting a question) to the front, ahead of TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A putto is a cherub figure, a little naked boy, in Renaissance painting.

clue.text: Exhausted state? Raise it with sign of embarrassment

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it bottom to top, turning it backwards

parts.note: blushing shows redness in the cheeks

explanation.surface: A tired person blushes when asked to bring something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' turns IT to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatigue is the condition of being worn out.

clue.text: Handles reminder of human mortality?

definitions.meaning: read as '...', a person growing older

explanation.surface: Coping with things reminds us we are getting older.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle something is to cope with or run it; split in two the word says a person grows old.

clue.text: Person declaiming liturgy runs round church the wrong way

indicators.note: the first pieces go round the church, enclosing it

parts.note: a rite is a liturgical ceremony

indicators.note: means the church abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A priest reading the service walks backwards about the chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liturgy' suggests the definition is a priest, but the person is simply one who declaims; RITE is a liturgical service.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who recites aloud, delivering a text to an audience.

clue.text: Quirk of bird artist captured

indicators.note: the bird holds the artist inside it, as a captor does

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter's oddity is to have caught a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A characteristic feature or peculiarity of someone's personality.

clue.text: Told stories about cricket side backed with gold sovereign once

indicators.note: the first word goes about the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: telling stories is lying

indicators.note: means the cricket side's name is read backwards

parts.note: the leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs
OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone lied about the cricket team, propped up with gold, back in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign once' points to a feudal ruler, not a coin; the leg side is cricket's on side, behind the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A feudal superior to whom vassals owed allegiance, a historical ruler or monarch.

clue.text: Neighbour of Carthage given nautical protection?

indicators.note: the word gives protection to the run of letters inside it, enclosing the town

explanation.surface: A North African town is guarded by the navy.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits within 'nautical'. Utica was an ancient Phoenician port near Carthage in modern Tunisia.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient city on the North African coast close to Carthage.

clue.text: Lacking support fouled our plan up

indicators.note: a fouled rope is tangled, so these letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Losing backing has messed up our scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Disliked and without popular backing.

clue.text: House plot developed in North-facing position

indicators.note: a developed site is rebuilt, so these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A building plot is developed with a northern outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North-facing' looks like estate-agent jargon, but at the earth's southernmost point every direction is north.
explanation.definitionFit: From the planet's southernmost point every way you look faces north.

clue.text: Excellent fish — like a large piece to start with?

indicators.note: puts the word for like a large piece first, ahead of the fish

parts.note: hunky describes something in a big hunk or chunk
the dory, or John Dory, is a sea fish

explanation.surface: A great fish dish is served in a big chunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start with' puts HUNKY ahead of DORY though the clue names the fish first.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal for fine, satisfactory, all well.

clue.text: How car approaches house — not in this, surely?

definitions.text: How car approaches house — not in this, surely?

parts.words: How car approaches house — not in this, surely?
parts.note: a car reaches a house by passing over the drive, yet one would not use the highest gear for that short stretch

explanation.surface: A car reaches a house up the driveway, slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest gear of a car, used for fast cruising rather than parking.

clue.text: Plant of primrose family, much sought after

definitions.meaning: the scarlet flower of that name is a member of the primula family
the Scarlet hero of Orczy's novel was sought here, there and everywhere

explanation.surface: A primula relative is in high demand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Scarlet Pimpernel's rhyme runs 'They seek him here, they seek him there'.
explanation.definitionFit: Names both a small red flower and the elusive, hunted hero of Baroness Orczy's novel.

clue.text: Born, an afterthought, to Swedes

parts.note: née means born, giving a married woman's maiden name
PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: A child arrives late in life to Scandinavian parents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swedes' looks like the people, but it is the root vegetable; NEEPS is the Scottish word for them, eaten with haggis.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots name for the turnip-like root vegetables, the yellow kind.

clue.text: Sly introduction for this intimidating husband's story

definitions.text: Sly introduction for this intimidating husband's story

parts.words: Sly introduction for this intimidating husband's story
parts.note: Christopher Sly is the tinker in the Induction to Shakespeare's comedy about taming a shrew, whose bullying hero is the husband

explanation.surface: A cunning opening to a tale of a domineering spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sly' looks like an adjective, but is Christopher Sly, for whom 'The Taming of the Shrew' is staged.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's suitor who tames Katherina by browbeating her.

clue.text: Poet has to embrace fool

indicators.note: the outer word wraps its arms round the inner, holding it inside

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A versifier must hug a clown.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was the Italian Renaissance author of 'Jerusalem Delivered'.

clue.text: Ask EU to alter arbitrary ruling

indicators.note: altering something changes it, so these letters are changed in order

explanation.surface: Brussels is asked to change a high-handed decision.
explanation.walkthrough: A UKASE was a Russian tsar's edict.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict from the tsar, hence any autocratic decree.

clue.text: Off-peak call

parts.note: sounds like a cheap-rate phone call, but it is a cry sent out from a mountain top

explanation.surface: A phone call made at the cheap rate.
explanation.definitionFit: The warbling Alpine shout between chest and falsetto voice made by mountain dwellers.

clue.text: Once it's crossed, no recall is possible

definitions.text: Once it's crossed, no recall is possible

parts.words: Once it's crossed, no recall is possible
parts.note: sounds like a point of no return, but describes a mythical underworld stream whose waters wipe away memory

explanation.surface: Some line, once passed, can never be revoked.
explanation.definitionFit: The underworld river of forgetfulness in Greek myth.

clue.text: Suitable place for a Callas extravaganza?

indicators.note: an extravagant show runs wild, so these letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A grand opera house suits the diva for a lavish show.
explanation.walkthrough: Maria Callas, the soprano, sang at this Milan opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan's opera house is an ideal venue for a great soprano.

clue.text: Mocking speaker's., merciless punch initially withheld

indicators.note: the opening letter of the second word is held back and left out

parts.note: an iron fist is ruthless force, a pitiless blow

explanation.surface: A sarcastic talker holds back a cruel blow at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially withheld' drops the F of FIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who uses irony, saying the opposite of what is meant.

clue.text: Stone giving edge on river — this one?

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it, so the stone comes after the river

parts.note: R is a map abbreviation for river
a hone is a whetstone that sharpens blades

explanation.surface: A sharpening stone puts an edge on a waterway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this one?' asks for a river, R and HONE giving the French one.
explanation.definitionFit: A major French waterway flowing from the Alps through Lyon to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Flowing sea — English charter party assembled here

parts.note: runny means liquid and flowing
the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A tide meets English signatories gathered for a document.
explanation.walkthrough: King John sealed Magna Carta at this Thames meadow in 1215.
explanation.definitionFit: The meadow where barons met King John to seal the Magna Carta.
